title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Vitruvius gold recovery: the carrier burns while gold persists into a different filtering cloth
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. An old gold-bearing garment is burned; mercury gathers the gold from its ashes, water is removed, and pressure through another cloth separates escaping mercury from retained gold. The valuable material persists while its original carrier is destroyed and a new tool appears.

source.span: VII.8.4, complete gold-bearing garment recovery paragraph, including both cloth roles
source.layer: Historical primary work in an explicitly named translation; source content inspected, no medieval Voynich ownership implied

differentiating_relation: GOLD belongs initially to GARMENT1; burning removes that carrier. GOLD then joins MERCURY in the residue; decanting removes WATER, and pressure through CLOTH2 lets MERCURY pass while GOLD remains. GARMENT1 and CLOTH2 cannot be silently identified.
complete_source_account: The source first names quicksilver as necessary to gild silver or copper.
It then changes to gold woven into a worn garment, followed by burning, water and mercury addition.
The rest after pouring off water is put into a cloth and squeezed; the source assigns the outgoing and retained materials separately.
known_counterexplanation: A transmutation account creates new gold from ashes. A one-cloth account reuses the destroyed garment as the filter. A generic straining account makes all contents leave together. Each destroys a different necessary participant or result relation.
